learning: Iteration 6 (70.83) showed mass 0.4 kg raised the score while line losses stayed at 1.0 on the s-bend and slalom. Yaw inertia is at its floor, so this race tests the footprint lever with the controller fixed.
notes: Iteration 7 package: the Builder's 8 mm footprint test on the iteration 6 best design (70.83). Only sensor_size changes, so the score difference is attributable to footprint.
rationale: The evidence is iteration 6 (70.83, best): mass 0.4 kg, body_length 0.16 m, 12 mm footprints, 0.06 m span, y 0.05 m, wheel_track 0.12 m. Its failure is unchanged: one line loss per run on the s-bend and slalom, with max_error 0.0641 and 0.0669 m, both at or above the 0.06 m off-track limit. Steering oscillation is low (0.133 and 0.148), so the robot is not over-turning. Earlier single-variable tests ruled out several levers: y 0.07 m did not remove the loss (iteration 3), body_length 0.12 m lowered the score (iteration 5), and the 0.016 m, wider-span design scored lowest (iteration 2, confounded). Mass has now been taken to its 0.4 kg minimum, so yaw inertia is exhausted, and the remaining single lever is sensor footprint. I adopt the Builder's geometry as proposed: sensor_size 0.008 m, with mass, body, positions, span and wheel geometry unchanged. The controller is held exactly at the iteration 6 values (kp 3.0, ki 0, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.5, last_direction, weights +1, +0.5, 0, -0.5, -1). Changing the gains now would confound the footprint test, and iteration 1 showed higher gain did not help. Risk: a smaller footprint lowers each sensor's reading when the robot is off-centre, so the sum of readings may fall below 0.05 sooner and produce more line-loss events. The 8 mm footprints still leave the 25 mm tape covered, since sensor spacing (0.015 m) is below the tape width. Expected result, as a prediction only: line losses on the s-bend and slalom fall below 1.0 and max_error drops under 0.06 m. The score should exceed 70.83, or the footprint is too small and the next step returns to 0.012 m.
